newsitem.title: KUWAIT: Kuwait says normal to request oil quota rise - paper.
newsitem.headline: Kuwait says normal to request oil quota rise - paper.

text.p: Kuwait's oil minister said in remarks published on Wednesday that it was normal for the Gulf Arab state to request an oil production quota increase.

"In view of what we have enjoyed in the past (larger output quota) and the modernisation and development to which we aspire, it is normal that we request an increase in our oil (production) quota," al-Anba newspaper quoted Isa al-Mazeedi as saying.

Kuwait often says it deserves a 200,000 bpd increase in its Organisation of Petroleum Exporting Countries (OPEC) production quota of 2.0 million bpd. Kuwait's output capacity stands at about 2.5 million bpd, officials say.

"We used to produce three million barrles per day (bpd) in the first half of 1973. It is unreasonable...(that) our production declines or falls at a time we find that our capacity is much higher than what we currently produce," Mazeedi said in an interview.
Mazeedi did not give details about the increase he envisaged nor the time in which such a request would be made.
